name: Question 1
problem:
Suppose we would like to find the maximum of the function $f(x,y,z)=x{y}^{2}z$ on the intersection of the surfaces ${x}^{2}-2{z}^{2}=1$ and ${y}^{2}+3{z}^{3}=5$ using the method of Lagrange multipliers. Then, the corresponding Lagrange multipliers $\lambda $ and $\mu $ satisfy the following system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}⟨{y}^{2}z,\,\bbox[2pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{AA}},\,x{y}^{2}⟩=\lambda ⟨2x,\,0,\,\bbox[2pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{AA}}\,⟩+\mu ⟨0,\,2y,\,\bbox[2pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{AA}}\,⟩ \\ {x}^{2}-2{z}^{2}=1 \\ {y}^{2}+3{z}^{3}=5\end{aligned}
$$

From left to right, what are the missing parts of the expressions?
worked_solution:
We need to find the maximum value of 

$$
f(x,y,z)=x{y}^{2}z
$$

 

subject to the constraints 

$$
g(x,y,z)={x}^{2}-2{z}^{2}=1,\,h(x,y,z)={y}^{2}+3{z}^{3}=5.
$$

Therefore, by the method of Lagrange multipliers, we must solve the following system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z)=\lambda ∇g(x,y,z)+\mu ∇h(x,y,z) \\ g(x,y,z)=1 \\ h(x,y,z)=5\end{aligned}
$$

We now expand the first equation of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & =\lambda ∇g(x,y,z)+\mu ∇h(x,y,z) \\ ⟨{f}_{x},{f}_{y},{f}_{z}⟩ & =\lambda ⟨{g}_{x},{g}_{y},{g}_{z}⟩+\mu ⟨{h}_{x},{h}_{y},{h}_{z}⟩ \\ ⟨{y}^{2}z,\,2xyz,\,x{y}^{2}⟩ & =\lambda ⟨2x,\,0,\,-4z⟩+\mu ⟨0,\,2y,\,9{z}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Suppose we would like to find the maximum of the function f(x,y,z)=xy2z on the intersection of the surfaces x2−2z2=1 and y2+3z3=5 using the method of Lagrange multipliers. Then, the corresponding Lagrange multipliers λ and μ satisfy the following system:

{⟨y2z,AA,xy2⟩=λ⟨2x,0,AA⟩+μ⟨0,2y,AA⟩x2−2z2=1y2+3z3=5

From left to right, what are the missing parts of the expressions?

a
2xyz, −4z, and 9z2
b
−2y, −4z, and 3z2
c
−2yz, 2x, and 3z3
d
2xyz, −2z2, and 3z2
e
y2z, −z2, and 3z2

We now expand the first equation of the system:

∇f(x,y,z)=λ∇g(x,y,z)+μ∇h(x,y,z)⟨fx,fy,fz⟩=λ⟨gx,gy,gz⟩+μ⟨hx,hy,hz⟩⟨y2z,2xyz,xy2⟩=λ⟨2x,0,−4z⟩+μ⟨0,2y,9z2⟩
